analysis.title: USA: Initial Claims Slightly Above Consensus Expectations
key_insights: Initial jobless claims rose 9k to 200k in the week ended November 7, slightly above the 194k median forecast and in line with GS at 200k. The prior week was revised to 191k.
The four-week moving average of initial claims was flat at 195k, the lowest level in the series' history.
Continuing claims fell 20k to 1,697k in the week ended October 31, slightly below the 1,710k median forecast. The prior week was revised to 1,717k.
Claims in Missouri jumped by 5k. GS suspects the spike will reverse next week, in line with previous large increases in Missouri claims this year.
Claims also rose 2k in California and New Jersey and fell 3k in Michigan.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Slightly above the 194k median forecast and in line with GS's 200k. Part of the rise is a Missouri jump that GS expects to reverse next week.

macro_indicators.indicator: Initial jobless claims, prior week revised
macro_indicators.interpretation: The 9k increase to 200k is measured from this revised level.
Flat on the prior reading and the lowest in the series' history, which points to a low pace of layoffs.
Down 20k and slightly below the 1,710k median forecast. Fewer people are receiving benefits through standard programs.

risk_factors: Missouri claims jumped 5k and may be distorting the headline initial claims figure. GS expects a reversal next week.
